title: The handoff contract
hook: A toy handoff pays repeated clarification or a one-time setup. Compare completed work.

knows: basic arithmetic and the meaning of a percentage
doesNotKnow: Distinguish a once-only setup cost from a repeated handoff cost before comparing total finished work.

misconception: A one-time delegation setup is wasteful whenever work could begin immediately.
objective: Distinguish a once-only setup cost from a repeated handoff cost before comparing total finished work.

claims.text: Original stipulated intervals model: A inputs [90, 20, 10] yield 60; B inputs [80, 20, 0] yield 80. Prediction correct option 80.00. A completes {A} work minutes; B {B}. B spends ten of the original ninety minutes once on setup, then avoids the repeated clarification charge. Setup and clarification costs are invented; the model does not assess whether expectations are complete.
claims.source: Original lesson construction; EDD-010 formula ; exact independent Python arithmetic recomputation recorded in answerCheck; no book dataset or measured human response.

claims.text: A toy handoff leaves 60 minutes after one-time setup. Each task needs 15 minutes and no repeated clarification. Work completed? Four complete fifteen-minute tasks fit; all sixty remaining minutes are work.
claims.source: Original transfer toy, intervals, inputs [60, 15, 0], output 60; independent Python recomputation.
